interpretation: Two augers (rods ~25 cm long, 25 mm diameter, dark end cap at the robot-side end, a collar ring at about 60% of the length). The doser (white plate obj3, motor block on the auger's -y side, red cube on the +y side) held a WHITE auger snapped into two snap clips (near clip x 0.358-0.372, far clip x 0.440-0.454, axis y 0.009, z 0.043; the clip lips wrap above the auger's equator). The blue auger rack (obj1, later split into agent objects) had two V-cradle slots, near cradle x 0.328-0.342 and far cradle x 0.448-0.464: slot A at y -0.165 held the LIGHT-BLUE (new) auger, and slot B at y -0.2345 was empty. Goal: the white auger rests in rack slot B, and the light-blue auger is snapped into both doser clips, in the same pose the white one had (axis z ~0.043, tip x ~0.50, collar between the clips). Ambiguities: how far along its axis each auger must be placed. I matched the original placements (tips at x 0.50, collars at x 0.41-0.42).
plan: Initial plan: grasp each auger from above at its tip end (x~0.49, the only spot that clears every clip on both fixtures and the motor block), with the gripper tilted 25 deg because straight-down was unreachable (joint5 limit). Carry it and place it. That changed once I saw that the parallel-jaw grip cannot hold the auger's weight torque from the tip: the auger pivoted in the fingers to 20-48 deg. The new plan was to lay the white auger back on top of the doser clip lips (not snapped) and regrasp it at its near end, between the end cap and the near clip (lever ~4 cm to the centre of mass). I placed it in rack slot B offset 3 cm toward the robot (that grasp point would otherwise hit the rack's near cradle), then pushed it along its axis into alignment. For the light-blue auger I used the same near-end grasp. Whenever the auger drooped in the grip, I levelled it by increasing the gripper pitch (alpha 15 -> 31-39 deg). I laid it on the doser's clip lips, released it, and snapped it in by pressing with the closed gripper. Last, I gripped its tip and pulled it 18 mm along its axis back to the original x position.

steps.what: Read embodiment (AgileX PiPER sim, 6 joints, parallel gripper stroke 0.07 m, cameras left/right/wrist), objects, renders, heightmaps, cross-sections of the clips; measured finger width from wrist depth (+-16 mm along TCP-x, tips ~25 mm past TCP).
steps.why: Locate the augers, clips, collar, motor block and red cube precisely, and find grasp spots that avoid them.
steps.result: Found that the doser clips are snap clips (lips at z 0.053-0.055 above the auger's equator) and the rack slots are open V cradles. The only grasp regions free on both fixtures are the tip end, and the near end only with an x offset. Agent objects were defined for the augers, block, rack and doser clips.

steps.what: IK scan: top-down at x 0.49 unreachable; chose tilt alpha 25 deg, grasp at x 0.492, TCP 6 mm above the axis. Executed the approach (step 102) and closed (reading 0.741, held).
steps.why: Tip-end grasp clears the far clip (x<=0.454) and the motor block.
steps.result: Good grasp on the white auger's tip end.

steps.what: Lift: +1.5 cm command (arm rose only 3.5 mm), then a +6.5 cm command.
steps.why: The snap clips resist; a larger position error makes the controller pull harder.
steps.result: Auger came out of both clips (step 200) but pivoted ~16-20 deg in the grip; its end cap fell onto the doser plate. Further lifts only steepened it (~30 deg, then ~48 deg). The grip cannot hold the weight torque from the tip.

steps.what: Lowered the tip grip back over the doser, so that the auger lay horizontal on top of the clip lips (axis z ~0.061, not snapped), then released (step ~438-472).
steps.why: Get the auger into a stable rest from which a grasp closer to its centre of mass is possible.
steps.result: White auger rested level on both clips' lips (top z 0.073), tip x 0.496.

steps.what: Regrasped at the near end (x 0.330, alpha 15 deg, TCP z 0.068: fingertips ~6 mm above the red cube, ~9 mm from the near clip). Closed (0.738) and lifted 3 cm.
steps.why: Lever to the centre of mass ~4 cm instead of ~12 cm.
steps.result: Auger lifted nearly level (~5 deg droop).

steps.what: Transported over rack slot B, aiming for tip x 0.472 (3 cm toward the robot so the fingers clear the rack's near cradle). Descended to z 0.075 (step 713).
steps.why: Place it in the empty slot.
steps.result: Auger drooped 17 deg tip-down in transit and its tip touched the rack. The TCP also sagged 7-12 mm from the command.

steps.what: Pitched the gripper alpha 15 -> 32 -> 37 deg and corrected the commanded y by -10 mm (from point-cloud circle fits), then lowered into the cradles and released (step 895).
steps.why: Level the auger in the grip and centre it on the slot.
steps.result: White auger rested in both V cradles of slot B: top z 0.057 (same as the light-blue originally), y -0.2348, tip x 0.471.

steps.what: Closed the gripper and pushed the end cap face +x in two pushes (steps 974-1084).
steps.why: Bring the white auger to the same axial position as the slot's original occupant.
steps.result: Tip x 0.5003, collar x 0.413-0.423, end cap from 0.251, still seated (top 0.057).

steps.what: Grasped the light-blue auger at its near end in slot A (x ~0.30, alpha 15 deg) and lifted (step 1214).
steps.why: Same near-end grasp, which over the doser is clear of the red cube (fingers closed on the auger are 8 mm inside it in y) and the near clip.

steps.what: Levelled it (alpha 31 then 39 deg), carried it over the doser, corrected x, and lowered it onto the clip lips (step 1399).
steps.why: Present it level and aligned over the clips.
steps.result: Rested on the lips, top z 0.075, y ~0.007, tip x 0.502.

steps.what: Tried to snap it by pushing down at the grip (step 1455).
steps.result: Failed: the push levered the auger (far end up), slid it +7 mm, and nothing snapped. Released (after one refused retract, I accidentally re-closed once, then reopened).

steps.what: Pressed the collar with the closed gripper: stage 1 (arm stalled 12 mm above target), stage 2 deeper command (step 1706).
steps.why: The collar lies between the clips, so the push loads both.
steps.result: Far clip snapped (top 0.056 there), but the auger pivoted and its near end rose.

steps.what: Pressed the near part at x ~0.336 (step 1827), then lifted off.
steps.result: Near clip snapped. The far end popped up at first, but once the press was released the whole auger settled snapped in both clips: top 0.054-0.055 along its full length (step 1891). It sat 18 mm too far +x (tip 0.518, collar against the far clip).

steps.what: Gripped the light-blue tip end (x ~0.493, alpha 25 deg) and pulled 13 mm, then 6 mm, along -x, then released and lifted (steps 2016-2175).
steps.why: Restore the original axial position (tip x 0.50, collar 0.41-0.42).
steps.result: Tip x 0.4998, collar 0.412-0.421, end cap 0.250-0.277, still snapped (top 0.053-0.056).

steps.what: Retracted the arm up (z 0.26), took final left/right/wrist images and cloud summaries, then called finish_episode at step 2224.
steps.why: Verify each part of the instruction from two or more cameras.
steps.result: Light-blue auger in both doser clips at the snapped height. White auger in the formerly empty rack slot. The light-blue auger's former slot is empty. Red cube and motor block undisturbed.

diagnosis: I believe the task succeeded. Residual risks if it is scored otherwise: (1) The scorer may use a tighter axial or position tolerance than I could check. The final positions match the originals to within ~1-2 mm by point-cloud extents (tips x 0.4998 and 0.5003), but these are perception estimates. (2) The snap state is inferred from geometry: the light-blue top is 0.053-0.056 along its length, axis ~0.042 against 0.043 originally. If the scorer instead needs a clip constraint to engage, I cannot see that. The doser and the rack were pushed hard at times (collar presses, axial pulls and pushes). Both looked unmoved in the images, but a small fixture shift would not be obvious.
lessons: 1) On this PiPER sim the parallel-jaw grip has low resistance to rotation about the closing axis: a 25 cm rod held 12 cm from its centre of mass pivots freely in the fingers. Grasp within ~4 cm of the centre of mass, and expect several degrees of droop that grows under transport accelerations. 2) Droop can be corrected afterwards by pitching the gripper (raise the tilt about the closing axis); the grip holds the rod's angle well enough for slow moves. 3) Snap clips need a large commanded position error (2-4 cm below or above contact) to generate enough force. Pushing outside the span between two clips levers the far end out. Pressing inside the span (on the collar) snaps the nearer clip first and the rod then settles; snapping one clip can pull its end in and lift the other. 4) Commanded vs actual TCP differs by up to ~1 cm near the reach limits and under load. Measure the actual TCP and the object's position from the cloud, then correct iteratively. 5) Straight-down approaches beyond x ~0.45 are unreachable (joint5 +-1.22 rad); 15-40 deg forward tilts work. Account for the tilted fingertips swinging toward +x when checking clearances. 6) Agent objects do not track moved objects: forget them after the object moves. 7) Always give retract motions enough duration: a refused preview followed by a gripper command re-closed the gripper on the object once.
